governanceNotes: Deliberate deferral, not an authored suggestion: Balint syndrome's functional sequelae (optic ataxia, oculomotor apraxia, simultanagnosia) have no honest catalog target. Mapping the syndrome to generic visual impairment would misrepresent the phenotype (acuity is typically preserved), and the case-series evidence base cannot support a defensible proposition for any other target.

Deliberate deferral, not an authored suggestion: Balint's syndrome is itself defined by the visuomotor outcomes a downstream edge would target (simultanagnosia, oculomotor apraxia, optic ataxia from bilateral occipito-parietal injury), so a Balint's-to-visual-impairment or blindness edge would largely restate the diagnostic presentation (the ME-41 phenotype-identity barrier), and the classic acquired-attention-deficit literature (Rizzo 1992, PMID 1529165) positions Balint's as a phenotype of dorsal-attention-network damage rather than a cause of an independent visual-acuity or field outcome; the dominant causal arrow runs into the identity (parieto-occipital lesions producing Balint's), not out of it.
